harbor_p24_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_001.text: Yue's last paid week began with an empty board at the contact desk. Han had cleared it for the final ordinary handover task, and the absence of papers looked strangely accusing. The traveler had imagined a last shift full of dramatic questions. Instead the first work was checking what should no longer be there. A canceled appointment notice, a stale room reference and a public copy with its date obscured each needed its own ordinary correction. Yue read them carefully. The twenty-sixth week had arrived without waiting for her to feel ready to stop.

harbor_p24_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_002.text: A woman came to ask whether the visitor's departure would close the household desk. Han answered from the actual ordinary office roster: the desk remained, with its staff and existing receiving routes. Yue's appointment was the bounded comparison work ending this week. The woman seemed relieved and then embarrassed, as if she had accidentally made the traveler unimportant. Yue told her the office's continuing presence was a good answer. The woman asked the question she had brought and found the assigned clerk. Yue watched them begin and felt both gladness and the small wound she had expected to hide better.

harbor_p24_003.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p24_003.text: You are allowed to be pleased that the desk continues and sorry that it continues without needing you at every table. Do not turn the second feeling into another project. We have the actual handover list for today. I want your observed field sources placed where the ordinary lead can find them, and your private notes kept private. The office does not own the way you remember supper or a frightening kettle. If you need a minute before opening the list, take it now. The first receiving hour begins soon, and you should eat before it does.

harbor_p24_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_004.text: Yue ate the bread she had bought privately and began the source comparison. The far-point account remained signed by its actual worker. Her own near-water observations were separate. The interpreter's six-copper test record identified its bounded hour and language scope. The pilot council notice reserved sixty-four once and named the final selection and reviews. She checked that no page called all three plans funded. The ordinary route lead accepted the files assigned to that duty. Han kept the wage and protected household sources at their proper desk.

harbor_p24_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_005.text: Rong Qu sent an ordinary reply about the collection keeper's winter availability. One proposed road date needed a later morning if the pilot were chosen. The council's approved plan allowed scheduling within the four return journeys after the keeper's actual acceptance; the route lead confirmed the change. Yue recorded the source during her first final half-day and handed it over. She did not keep the question open solely because she would not attend the journey. Across the water, Lu Lian had already received the permitted status about her son.

harbor_p24_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_006.text: At the maintenance office, the technical keeper showed the repair pilot's current sample and the independently checked fitting. It remained an eligible plan, not purchased work. The sample belonged to ordinary demonstration stock and would not follow Yue out of town. The four unused port stones stayed in their secured store, with the exhausted drill and storm pairs separately logged. Sui asked the keeper to show the actual count rather than repeat it from memory. Yue observed only the public custody summary she was assigned to compare. The screen frame's ownership remained the port's, as it had always been.

harbor_p24_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_007.text: The keeper opened the stock book and named four unused stones, four exhausted, eight bought for sixteen. The remaining emergency cash was sixty-eight in its distinct categories, not four stones priced into a second balance. Nothing in the final appointment returned that reserve to Yue's account. The technical keeper would carry readiness forward under the existing role and any future actual approval. Sui closed the book and asked whether the ordinary lane was clear. It was. She went outside to watch a rope task rather than make another speech about limited power. The tide had no need to applaud inventory.

harbor_p24_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_008.text: Yan completed the next supervised inspection exercise under the independent officer's role. The result's conditions had not vanished because Yue's appointment approached its end. He compared the support source with the active use sheet and stopped when an unresolved concern required technical attention. The officer confirmed the correct action for that exercise and retained the actual record. Bo waited beyond the work boundary, trying to look patient. When Yan returned, he asked whether wisdom had passed. The foreman said the check had, and wisdom would need another appointment. They laughed and began the ordinary rigging task still theirs to perform.

harbor_p24_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_009.text: Deren saw Yue at the canteen and invited her to admire the cup one last time before leaving. She said there were several days yet. He answered that a magnificent rim could not be reviewed too often. She sat. He told her the twenty-six had gone where he needed it, and his compatible work continued under its actual hours. He had eaten with Yan again. He gave no details beyond wanting her to know the conversation was possible. Yue thanked him. They spent the rest of lunch arguing whether the cup's color resembled a civilized sea or an unfortunate cabbage.

harbor_p24_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_010.text: Ke Chun brought her new shears to the partnership room for her own small private mending after the paid work interval ended. The employer's task tools were already returned to their keeper. He Ming asked whether she wanted tea. Ke did, and told the partners she might eventually consider another trade role if stitching demand returned. The statement made An anxious about the guaranteed schedule. She reminded him her current accepted hours would be performed or changed through the actual terms. Future possibility was not notice of abandonment.

harbor_p24_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_011.text: The partnership's second guaranteed batch closed during this week under the same ninety-six structure. The advance and balance paid its actual materials twenty-four, space sixteen and wages forty-eight, leaving another earned eight margin. The first reserve had six remaining after tying stock; the new eight made fourteen. The partners kept it for bounded venture needs by agreement. The final two guaranteed batches remained future work, not earned cash. He Ming wrote the actual closeout while Ke counted the wage she was due.

harbor_p24_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_012.text: Wu arrived with ordered food after her canteen stock shift. She asked whether the scratch had been approved by the superintendent gull. An said it had signed with a wing. Ke said the board's handwriting was now better than the founders'. They laughed until Zhou reminded them the next actual order still needed a reply. Wu stayed only long enough for lunch; her children expected her at the agreed hour. The business could miss her and still respect the wage and household she had chosen.

harbor_p24_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_013.text: The duck had stolen the older child's new name for it by responding only when food appeared, regardless of the sound. The child declared all names useless and spent an afternoon calling the bird Chair. Wu said this had produced the family's most reliable conversation about property. He Ming laughed and promised Jun the story in her next private letter. Yue, seated near the window by invitation after work, enjoyed hearing a household continue to manufacture foolishness while official projects closed.

harbor_p24_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_014.text: Fen's apprenticeship supervisor gave her a task she could complete independently, with the trained check still required before dispatch. The girl felt trusted and frightened of losing trust through a mistake. Aning told her the mistake was already forming somewhere and should be welcomed before it learned to hide. Fen accused her of becoming the aunt. They laughed. The task went well after checking. At supper Luo listened to the account, including the error she nearly made. He said he liked the part where she had asked a question. She said that part paid the same wage as the others.

harbor_p24_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_015.text: Luo's later light-work start remained after the harbor's final season checks. He had paid the ordinary private booking deposit and kept his own accepted work copy. The rest of the fare would be paid from his earnings under the actual licensed route. Fen would stay for the apprenticeship and her own room arrangement. They examined the household objects again, deciding the kettle could remain because she used it more. He wanted to take the old fishing line. She asked whether light record sorting required fishing. He said homesickness did. She laughed, then cried before either could improve the answer.

harbor_p24_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_016.text: Her father let her cry without canceling the plan in order to make the evening immediately kind. Afterward he asked whether she wanted him to save supper while she washed her face. She did. The ordinary bowl waited. Their private contact arrangement named receiving places and permissions they actually accepted, rather than a promise he would send every thought at a fixed hour forever. Fen wanted more certainty and understood why nobody could buy it by writing a neater sentence. The next morning she went to the shop, where the aunt asked about a column, not the household's entire future.

harbor_p24_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_017.text: Aning's paid task for her father's shop took place in an interval cleared against her aunt's work commitment. She checked the agreed account scope and received the stated private fee on completion. Her father said paying his own daughter felt strange. She said being expected to work free had felt strange too, but they had tolerated it for years. He frowned, then laughed reluctantly. They had supper without discussing the fee again. Family had not become a market merely because one actual task acquired honest terms. The father still tried to give her an unnecessary warning about the road home.

harbor_p24_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_018.text: Han's last comparison meeting with Yue took place in the back room rather than a public ceremony. The desk lead accepted the completed source list and identified the receiving duties. Unresolved questions had keepers, dates and routes; they were not bundled into a command for the departing visitor to stay reachable forever. Yue signed her own task completion, Han hers. They looked at the empty space where the checked-out board would no longer rest. The clerk said it would probably acquire somebody else's untidy cup by tomorrow. Yue hoped it did, and discovered the hope felt less like defeat now.

harbor_p24_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_019.text: The loan keeper read the checkout list against the objects returned: boards, task pencils, form supplies and permitted office packets. Used consumables were recorded as used; unused task stock returned to its actual store. Yue's personal cup, notebook, ordinary blade and wrapped pendant did not enter the office's property column. No portrait, cabinet, screen stone or demonstration tool became hers by association. The keeper accepted the reconciliation and gave the ordinary receipt. Yue tucked her own copy among personal travel papers. The returned board looked strangely bare in his hands, as if it had expected another morning at her table.

harbor_p24_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_020.text: She had sharpened the blade earlier for maintenance and now used it to trim a thread on her pack at lodging. The task required no new property or rank. Her pendant stayed wrapped among possessions, never entered as purchased fuel or emergency stock. She folded the bedding and then unfolded it because she still needed the bed for the final paid week. The familiar objects were patient with her indecision. Outside, a cart squealed past the window and somebody argued about onions. The harbor sounded less like a project ending than a place where work would begin without her tomorrow.

harbor_p24_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_021.text: Before the final source meeting, Yue visited the near-water landing on a private walk along the shore, without crossing or charging a fare. The repaired line remained under its ordinary keeper's checks. The onion seller recognized her and asked whether the road plan had won. No final choice had been made. The woman said committees enjoyed leaving vegetables uncertain. Yue asked what she preferred. She wanted the registry because her deliveries took her past it, and wished the road visits could somehow cost less. The two opinions fit easily inside one person whose basket had already made enough trouble.

harbor_p24_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_022.text: The older passenger from the delayed ferry sat near the public step with a cane and a parcel. He had waited for a nephew who misunderstood the hour. Yue offered to read the clock notice, then stayed for a conversation after he said he needed no official help. He asked why cultivators always looked as though their next road mattered enormously. She laughed and said he might have selected the wrong examples. He answered that she had spent ten minutes gazing at a rope like it represented destiny. The remark was unfair and close enough to make her laugh again.

harbor_p24_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_023.text: His nephew arrived with an apology and the wrong-sized cover for the parcel. The older man complained that family had become skilled at appearing after the difficult part. Yue stepped aside while they arranged the load between them. The nephew offered a private thanks, which she accepted, and they went inland by the ordinary safe road. She remained at the landing another minute, this time looking deliberately at an unimportant gull. It stole a small scrap from the quay and flew away without reference to her future. The harbor's capacity for irrelevance felt unexpectedly comforting.

harbor_p24_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_024.text: At Wen's workshop, the ordinary rack held a sound modest load. Yue had come by invitation to drink tea, not inspect the repair after its claim closed. Wen asked whether the traveler wanted a tub as a parting gift. Yue stared until the woman laughed. She had chosen the largest container for the joke. The habitual pack could not contain it, and no gift was actually offered. They drank tea and discussed Wen's next private order. The workshop would stay busy after the public case became somebody else's story. Wen hoped it became a shorter story soon.

harbor_p24_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_025.text: Peng arrived to examine a future door task under an actual customer inquiry. He asked Wen why the traveler looked suspicious. She said Yue feared being given a tub. The carpenter said a lid would be more portable and equally unwelcome. They laughed. He kept the future task separate from work already paid and returned no borrowed tool to the wrong owner. Yue watched him measure and then left before the ordinary work became another reason to stay. The afternoon belonged to private visits, whose timing she could choose because the roster named only two bounded half-days this week.

harbor_p24_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_026.text: He Ming showed Yue the second batch's notebook before it closed, by her own consent as a friend. The buyer's substitute appointment was confirmed, actual stock ready and wages due through the accepted balance. The venture's first six reserve remained until the second earned margin arrived. Yue asked what He Ming feared now. She said she feared success making everybody pretend the first losses had been necessary lessons. She would have preferred dry wrapping and a sound neighboring roof. They laughed without denying how much the table had changed. A new room could be welcome without making the fire useful.

harbor_p24_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_027.text: Zhou overheard and said the landlord should reduce the new rent because the partnership now brought philosophical conversation to the neighborhood. An replied that philosophy would charge extra for storage. Ke asked whether her actual wage included listening to founders discuss themselves. He Ming said no and apologized, then asked about the checking task instead. Ke smiled. They returned to work with the employee's instructions clear. Yue sat outside the production lane finishing her privately bought tea. A friend's welcome did not mean she had to observe every fold until a room looked like an illustration of growth.

harbor_p24_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_028.text: Wu's canteen supervisor asked whether she wanted a further ordinary stock task during the cold months. The proposed rate and hours were real; she would consider them against childcare and the existing duties she liked. He Ming heard this and asked whether more work would leave less time for tea. Wu said yes on some evenings and wanted the partnership to stop treating her absence as a tragedy. The founder laughed, chastened. Friendship would have to use actual available hours, like everything else in lives where children and employers had not agreed to coordinate themselves for its convenience.

harbor_p24_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_029.text: The duck had apparently accepted Chair as a name because the children now shouted it while carrying food. Wu's neighbor said this meant the bird was better at contracts than most adults. He had once resented its noise and now defended it against a visiting cousin who called it filthy. Wu appreciated the loyalty and cleaned the basket herself. The household's small alliance had grown through practical help rather than a grand decision to belong. Yue visited supper by invitation, paying her own agreed share of ingredients when asked, and listened to the children argue over whether furniture could migrate.

harbor_p24_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_030.text: The younger child asked if Yue would take the toy boat on her road. Wu said the toy belonged to the children, and they had not decided to give it. Yue said she wanted to remember it here, where it had survived the washbasin and duck. The child considered this insufficiently heroic but kept the boat. Its ordinary patched hull would remain with the household. The traveler acquired no optional harbor object through a casual compliment. She helped clear bowls using the household's water and went home with the same habitual pack, a private meal and one more absurd story.

harbor_p24_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_031.text: At Han's room, the personal notebook shelf had begun collecting a tiny dust line where the book usually stood. Yue cleaned it with the clerk's cloth after asking, then realized she was rehearsing absence. Han noticed and said the shelf might acquire a plant once the book left. Yue asked whether the plant could write road replies. The clerk said only if it received enough water and a decent fee. They laughed. Han's future room was hers to rearrange. The traveler could be missed without leaving a physical hollow everybody agreed never to fill.

harbor_p24_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_032.text: Duan visited Han's room for private tea and saw the imperfect painted curve beside the gull. She liked the curve better now than when it was made because the clerk had continued practicing instead of worshiping the first decent stroke. Han said artists gave alarming compliments. The painter asked whether her future lettering schedule remained secondary to actual clerk duties. It did. They discussed a possible later task without calling it a commission yet. Yue listened while two women planned work that would continue after she left, then discovered she could enjoy that conversation without measuring her place inside it.

harbor_p24_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_033.text: The dog's keeper called from the lane to say the animal had again stolen a rag. Duan put down her cup with the expression of an artist whose main rival possessed teeth. Han offered no office authority over the offender. Yue joined the private search after the keeper said the route was safe and no work area needed entering. They found the rag beneath an empty bench and the dog pretending innocence nearby. Duan retrieved it and thanked them. The small pursuit filled ten minutes that no appointment paid for, and everybody returned to tea in a better mood.

harbor_p24_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_034.text: Qin's sister sent the disputed song line in her own handwriting. He brought it to the stall and asked everyone to admit it was wrong. Han said the line scanned better than his. The replacement custodian agreed, which made Qin accuse him of disloyalty and then laugh. Yue knew neither version and refused the appointed role of impartial judge. They sang both badly enough to distress a fish seller. The seller threatened to charge for lost customers. Qin bought a small portion as compensation by private agreement, proving bad music could generate a business expense without becoming a public remedy.

harbor_p24_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_035.text: The old man spoke again about a shorter role after his employer considered staffing. The future arrangement had no final approval yet, and he was content to wait for the actual answer while performing his current duties. He told Yue he had spent years believing the next difficult case would determine when he could rest. Cases kept arriving. She recognized the habit and said nothing for a while. Qin asked if that meant she had become wise. She said it meant she was eating fish. He approved the practical answer and changed the subject to his garden.

harbor_p24_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_036.text: At the warehouse's ordinary reopening, Hao kept the public explanation to cleared sections, corrected access and current reporting. She did not offer a permanent guarantee against danger. The smaller footprint affected rent and future stock, which her steward still disliked. He had begun counting actual maintenance hours instead of only the income column. Bao chose not to attend the opening celebration and sent a permitted ordinary message wishing the current workers well. Her injury payment and care did not bind her to perform forgiveness in the yard. Hao read the message privately and accepted its size.

harbor_p24_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_037.text: The cloth trader's daughter visited the reopened warehouse to price a future modest shelf. She inspected the current terms and chose not to rent yet because her private space still suited the restarted trade. The keeper accepted the refusal without asking whether the earlier forty-four settlement had purchased loyalty. Her father came afterward and asked about the new door turn. It worked for his load. He grunted approval and went back to his shop. A repaired place could earn ordinary trust one use at a time, without requiring each former customer to sign a declaration that fear had ended.

harbor_p24_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_038.text: Bao's next net task had a later deadline and her actual accepted rate. Dai asked whether the care interval fit before assigning it. Bao accepted the part she could do, refused the heavier portion and felt proud of neither answer until the work began. Then the familiar motion steadied her. She wanted someday to return to sorting or another ordinary role, but current wishes did not grant medical clearance. Her cousin left her alone for the short interval Bao requested and returned when agreed. The house could be quiet without turning quiet into abandonment.

harbor_p24_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_039.text: Ke's shears cut a household patch cleanly after the employer's paid day ended. She had bought them from her funds and tool-claim payment, and no office expected their return. Tong asked whether she planned to pursue the further route about the unsupported part of the bag. She had not decided. The notice remained available. He said he would give the truthful account again if properly asked. They no longer needed to reopen their unsafe return at every meeting. She handed him the jacket's sleeve and said it had cost a cup of tea, payable now rather than through a committee.

harbor_p24_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_040.text: Tong bought the tea and complained that she charged interest in insults. Ke said only for repeat customers. Their laughter caught Yue's attention as she passed on a private walk, and she was invited to sit. She did not ask for the claim's whole history again. Ke showed the shears, Tong the repaired sleeve, and the three spoke about ordinary work. The traveler had been present for difficult receiving hours, but these people could now choose what to tell her over a cup. They were not a permanently open file assigned to make her departure emotionally complete.

harbor_p24_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_041.text: The final public referral comparison found the office's receiving room open and its ordinary covering clerk present. Yue checked the actual schedule and marked the bounded task finished. A new claimant asked if she could take his papers because she looked familiar from the pilot notice. She directed him to the assigned keeper rather than create private custody outside her ending role. He accepted the route after Han greeted him by the actual intake question. Yue stood aside. The ordinary desk began the next case without asking the departing visitor to approve its first sentence.

harbor_p24_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_042.text: During her last private practice before term closeout, Yue formed the familiar earned pairs on the permitted dry strip, moved the marker within its measured range and released before strain. Stage four remained stage four. She rested with her own cup and watched a carpenter's cart pass beyond the boundary. There was no secret reward in the week's orderly accounts. She had steadier habits, friendships and pay earned through actual work. The next town would meet those things in an ordinary traveler, whose powers still required safe tasks and whose ordinary feet still needed a road.

harbor_p24_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_043.text: Sui asked whether Yue would submit a note about the pilot's first review after leaving. The traveler said she could offer no promised visit or work interval. She might write from a receiving place when travel allowed, and the keeper should run the review without relying on her. The captain accepted and thanked her for the answer. Then she admitted the request had been partly a way to keep a thread. Yue smiled and said friendship could hold a thread without tying it to a maintenance report. They agreed an ordinary private contact would be kinder than a disguised commission.

harbor_p24_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_044.text: The council's maintenance keeper confirmed the final selection meeting in week twenty-seven. Sixty-four remained reserved and unspent. Registry, repair and road had their eligible plans and accepting keepers; the first review would be four weeks after launch, closeout eight. The public notice's existing-rights clause stayed visible. Deren read it again, then said he still wanted repair covers. He Ming still wanted road visits. Han still liked the index cabinet and now admitted it without apology. Their preferences could survive the ordinary closing of Yue's appointment because the committee had funded a future they themselves would inhabit.

harbor_p24_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_045.text: At the last source table, Yue named the keepsake she would actually carry: her personal notes. They contained reflections and permitted details she had authority to retain, not copies of protected official files she had taken for memory. Han helped her compare the boundary once, without reading passages about their room. The notebook remained Yue's, and the household records remained the office's. The clerk handed back the personal book and teased her about its uneven binding. Yue said it had survived her writing. Han said survival was a low standard, then offered the needle she owned for a mending task.

harbor_p24_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_046.text: Yue used the household needle by permission and returned it after repairing the notebook cover. Han did not give it as an unasked parting object. The traveler had enough ordinary possessions to pack and enough memories without adding a tool she could borrow next time. They drank tea in the room whose renewed lease Han had chosen. The shelf still held the book for this visit. Tomorrow, after the term receipt, Yue would begin the private week she had paid for. The clerk asked whether that changed their planned evening walk. It did not.

harbor_p24_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_047.text: The canteen's turnips finally became sweet enough that Bo accused the cook of switching suppliers to defeat a longstanding joke. Wu said the stock task showed the same source, and weather had apparently chosen to cooperate with taste. Deren demanded a technical hearing on the subject. Yan said he was currently available only for supervised opinions. Their laughter rose across the room. Yue sat with them by private invitation after work, paying for her own bowl. The meal felt like part of a life she could leave without pretending it had been created solely to teach her how to go.

harbor_p24_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_048.text: When the private gathering ended, Yue walked back with He Ming as far as the partnership's new doorway. The sign Han made was plain and legible under the ordinary light. Inside, the ugly gull waited above a table scratched by actual work. He Ming said she had once wanted this business to prove her household no longer needed anyone. Now she wanted it to pay its people and leave them able to need one another honestly. Yue did not answer with a lesson. She squeezed her friend's hand, then went on to the room where the last paid night waited.

harbor_p24_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_049.text: At the lodging doorway, the keeper confirmed the final term invoice and the separate seven-night receipt. Yue would keep the same bed through week twenty-seven under a different payment source. The keeper asked whether she wanted breakfast ordered for the first morning. She did, at the stated customer price from her own purse. The detail made leaving the appointment feel more concrete than signing its last page. She had been a guest before every commission and would be a guest after this one. Upstairs, her familiar cup sat beside notes she no longer had to open for work at dawn.

harbor_p24_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_050.text: The operations keeper approved the final appointment account after twenty-eight completed half-days. Wages totaled fifty-six, bed and meals eighty-four, ferries eighteen, copying fourteen and interpretation twelve. Spending was one hundred eighty-four from the separately approved two hundred. The sixteen unspent returned to operations control: ferry six, copies four, interpretation six. The old appointment's forty-four remained its own already closed return. No remainder funded the maintenance pilot or private travel. Yue received the last four wage copper for the week's two half-days, and the final six bed invoice was paid under the stated term.

harbor_p24_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_051.text: Han checked the return receipt and asked Yue whether she wanted the completion description read once. It said the appointment had compared routes and preserved sources through its bounded duties. It did not claim every problem solved or every household happy. The traveler smiled at the modest words and then frowned at the word completed beside her name. The desk's work remained unfinished because desks continued. Her particular agreement had ended. Han waited while she understood the difference emotionally, then offered the tea she had bought with money. The office owed no extra shift merely because the kettle was warm.

harbor_p24_052.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p24_052.text: Your twenty-eight half-days are done. Tomorrow the appointment pays no bed, meals or visitor wage. You have said you want a private stay through the final harbor checks and pilot selection. Make that arrangement with the lodging keeper from your own earned money, with the price stated, so nobody extends the term out of kindness. You can still come for tea by invitation. The desk will decide its ordinary tasks without putting your name on the roster. I will miss seeing it there. I also want us to be friends when no institution is paying for the room around us.

harbor_p24_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_053.text: Yue arranged seven more nights with the lodging keeper at the ordinary stated private price of fourteen copper for bed only. She paid from her own earned money before the new interval began in week twenty-seven. Meals would be private purchases or invitations agreed by friends, not hidden in the former six-copper weekly bed-and-meal invoice. Her appointment had earned fifty-six in this term and forty-eight in the first, with earlier personal travel money kept separately. The private fourteen reduced her purse, not either public balance. She asked for the ordinary receipt and then went to buy supper.

harbor_p24_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_054.text: At the tea stall she found Qin speaking with the replacement custodian about a shorter future role. Their employer would consider it under its own staffing needs; no decision had been made merely because the old man wanted mornings for beans. Yue told them her term had closed. Qin raised his cup and said she had now entered the respectable profession of paying for lodging herself. She said she had extensive prior experience and poor references from her purse. The younger custodian laughed. They shared a private bowl and discussed the song's last line, which remained magnificently unsupported by evidence.

harbor_p24_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_055.text: Sui took the completion status to the port handover only insofar as it affected receiving routes. The pilot's sixty-four stayed reserved at the maintenance keeper, unspent until the final choice. Four unused stones remained secure; emergency cash sixty-eight retained its purposes. Her supervisory reviews continued beyond Yue's departure. The captain saw no reason to dress these facts as farewell. She invited the traveler to supper instead and made a flat bread that came out sound on the first attempt. Yue praised it with enough surprise to offend her. Sui demanded better manners from a guest with no official duties left.

harbor_p24_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_056.text: At supper Sui asked what Yue would do if the next town had no useful work. The traveler said she would ask questions, inspect terms and keep enough of her earned money for the road. She had no inherited kiln post, guard commission or portable harbor authority. Sui nodded and changed the subject to her son's ovens. The conversation pleased Yue because advice had ended before becoming an attempt to control the route. They ate food in the captain's room while a neighbor knocked to borrow a bowl, receiving it under the ordinary loan nobody needed to call a policy.

harbor_p24_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_057.text: The last evening of the paid term, Han and Yue walked past the pilot notice. Registry, repair and road still waited as three eligible alternatives for one sixty-four. The keepers had accepted the work, first review four weeks after launch and closeout eight. Existing claims and rights continued regardless of selection. Yue would spend her private week among friends and the final choice, then leave. Han touched the paper's curled edge and did not straighten it until she asked the keeper. The pause made them laugh. The clerk had become conscientious about even a notice that had already been checked.

harbor_p24_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p24_058.text: Yue returned to her room and put the appointment receipt beside the private lodging one. The two papers named different agreements, both real. She packed the objects she would not use before morning and left the bedding open. Her personal notes contained no official file borrowed under an unreturned pretext. On the last page she wrote that the term had ended at one hundred eighty-four spent and sixteen returned. Then she added a line about the captain's good bread. Tomorrow would begin a week no office purchased for her, in a harbor she could finally visit without being its employee.
